entries.title: Remove the SMBv1 protocol
entries.description: Ensures the legacy SMBv1 optional feature (client and server) is not installed.
entries.rationale: SMBv1 has no signing or encryption and is the WannaCry/EternalBlue vector. Windows 11 does not install it by default, but users can re-add it for old devices.

managedBy.groupPolicyPath: Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\MS Security Guide\Configure SMB v1 server

sideEffects: Legacy NAS, printers or scanners that only speak SMBv1 become unreachable until replaced or updated.

entries.title: Require SMB signing (client and server)
entries.description: Forces the SMB client and server to sign every connection so traffic cannot be tampered with in transit.
entries.rationale: Blocks SMB relay and man-in-the-middle tampering. Windows 11 24H2 requires signing by default; older builds and upgraded machines often do not.

managedBy.groupPolicyPath: Computer Configuration\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Local Policies\Security Options\Microsoft network client: Digitally sign communications (always)

sideEffects: Third-party servers that do not sign SMB (older NAS, some Samba configs, scan-to-SMB MFPs) fail with a signing-mismatch error.
Small throughput reduction on 1 GbE and faster links.

entries.title: Disable multicast DNS (mDNS)
entries.description: Turns off the Windows mDNS responder so the machine no longer answers or issues .local multicast queries.
entries.rationale: mDNS is an attacker-spoofable name-resolution channel similar to LLMNR. Disabling it removes another local poisoning surface; requires a Dnscache service restart.
sideEffects: Breaks discovery of Bonjour/AirPrint printers, Chromecast/AirPlay devices, HomeKit, Sonos and hostname.local resolution.

entries.title: Disable NetBIOS over TCP/IP on public networks
entries.description: Uses the Configure NetBIOS settings policy to turn off NetBIOS name resolution on networks classified as public.
entries.rationale: NetBIOS name resolution is spoofable (NBT-NS poisoning). Disabling it on public networks removes the attack surface where it is riskiest while keeping workgroup name resolution on trusted LANs.

managedBy.groupPolicyPath: Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Network\DNS Client\Configure NetBIOS settings

sideEffects: Legacy name resolution and Network Neighborhood browsing over public networks stop working.

entries.title: Disable NetBIOS over TCP/IP on all networks
entries.description: Turns off NetBIOS name resolution on every network and sets the node type to P-node so the machine never broadcasts NetBIOS queries.
entries.rationale: Fully removes the NBT-NS poisoning surface (the 25H2 baseline default). P-node prevents broadcast name resolution entirely.

managedBy.groupPolicyPath: Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Network\DNS Client\Configure NetBIOS settings

sideEffects: Name resolution by NetBIOS name (old NAS/printers, UNC names in workgroups without DNS or mDNS) and Network Neighborhood browsing break on all networks.

entries.title: Disable WPAD proxy auto-discovery
entries.description: Sets the documented Disable WPAD switch so WinHTTP no longer auto-discovers a proxy via DHCP/DNS.
entries.rationale: WPAD auto-discovery lets a network attacker advertise a malicious proxy and intercept traffic. Home networks do not use WPAD.
sideEffects: Networks that rely on WPAD/PAC proxy auto-discovery lose Internet until a proxy is set manually.

entries.title: Turn off smart multi-homed name resolution
entries.description: Stops Windows from sending DNS queries out every interface in parallel, so only the preferred interface's DNS is used.
entries.rationale: Parallel multi-homed resolution leaks DNS queries outside a VPN tunnel and lets a rogue interface answer first. Disabling it prevents the leak.

managedBy.groupPolicyPath: Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Network\DNS Client\Turn off smart multi-homed name resolution

sideEffects: Slower or failed name resolution in multi-NIC or VPN setups where the primary DNS is unreachable.

entries.title: Allow and auto-upgrade to DNS over HTTPS
entries.description: Sets the DoH policy to allow encrypted DNS and auto-upgrade to it whenever the configured resolver is known to support DoH.
entries.rationale: Encrypts DNS queries against on-path tampering and eavesdropping. Allow/auto-upgrade is safe because it falls back to plaintext when the resolver is not DoH-capable.

managedBy.groupPolicyPath: Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Network\DNS Client\Configure DNS over HTTPS (DoH) name resolution

sideEffects: Encrypted DNS can bypass local DNS-filtering appliances.

entries.title: Harden the TCP/IP stack (source routing, ICMP redirects, name release)
entries.description: Applies the MSS network hardening values: block IPv4/IPv6 source routing, ignore ICMP redirects, and refuse NetBIOS name-release requests.
entries.rationale: These MSS-legacy settings block classic spoofing and route-hijack tricks. No realistic breakage on modern networks.

managedBy.groupPolicyPath: Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\MSS (Legacy)\MSS: (DisableIPSourceRouting) IP source routing protection level

entries.title: Enable Safe DLL search mode
entries.description: Pins Safe DLL search mode so the system directories are searched before the current directory when a process loads a DLL.
entries.rationale: Mitigates DLL-preloading/hijack attacks that drop a malicious DLL in the working directory. Enabled by default; this pins the safe state.

managedBy.groupPolicyPath: Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\MSS (Legacy)\MSS: (SafeDllSearchMode) Enable Safe DLL search mode

entries.title: Restrict anonymous and null-session access
entries.description: Blocks anonymous enumeration of SAM accounts and shares, removes Everyone-includes-anonymous, restricts remote SAM access to administrators, and disables null-session fallback.
entries.rationale: Anonymous/null-session access lets an unauthenticated attacker enumerate accounts and shares for reconnaissance. The STIG rates several of these CAT I.

managedBy.groupPolicyPath: Computer Configuration\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Local Policies\Security Options\Network access: Do not allow anonymous enumeration of SAM accounts and shares

sideEffects: Old multi-function printers that scan-to-share via null sessions, and legacy apps that enumerate shares anonymously, stop working.

entries.title: Enable Windows Firewall on all profiles
entries.description: Turns the Windows Defender Firewall on for the Domain, Private and Public profiles via policy.
entries.rationale: A running firewall on every profile is the baseline network defense. Policy values keep it enabled even if a tool or malware tries to turn it off.

managedBy.groupPolicyPath: Computer Configuration\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Windows Defender Firewall with Advanced Security\Windows Defender Firewall Properties\Domain Profile\Firewall state

entries.title: Firewall default: block inbound, allow outbound
entries.description: Sets the default action to block unsolicited inbound connections and allow outbound on all three firewall profiles.
entries.rationale: Blocking inbound by default is the core firewall posture; anything not explicitly allowed is dropped.

managedBy.groupPolicyPath: Computer Configuration\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Windows Defender Firewall with Advanced Security\Windows Defender Firewall Properties\Domain Profile\Inbound connections

entries.title: Enable firewall logging (dropped and successful) on all profiles
entries.description: Logs dropped packets and successful connections with a 16 MB log file on each firewall profile.
entries.rationale: Firewall logs are essential forensic data after a network intrusion. Disk impact is negligible.

managedBy.groupPolicyPath: Computer Configuration\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Windows Defender Firewall with Advanced Security\Windows Defender Firewall Properties\Domain Profile\Logging

sideEffects: Firewall log files grow up to 16 MB per profile.

entries.title: Public profile: ignore local firewall rules
entries.description: On the Public profile, applies only domain/GPO firewall and IPsec rules and ignores locally created rules.
entries.rationale: Prevents apps (and malware) from opening inbound holes on untrusted networks by adding their own local rules.

managedBy.groupPolicyPath: Computer Configuration\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Windows Defender Firewall with Advanced Security\Windows Defender Firewall Properties\Public Profile\Settings\Apply local firewall rules

sideEffects: Apps can no longer add their own inbound firewall rules on the Public profile; some games/VoIP prompts will not appear.

entries.title: Firewall notifications: prompt on Private/Domain, silent on Public
entries.description: Keeps the allow-an-app prompt on the Domain and Private profiles and suppresses it on the Public profile so blocked apps are dropped silently.
entries.rationale: Matches the Microsoft baseline: users get prompts on trusted networks but untrusted networks never surface a prompt that could be click-allowed.

managedBy.groupPolicyPath: Computer Configuration\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Windows Defender Firewall with Advanced Security\Windows Defender Firewall Properties\Public Profile\Settings\Display a notification

sideEffects: The Public profile no longer prompts when a program starts listening; it is blocked silently.

entries.title: Turn off Remote Assistance (solicited and offered)
entries.description: Disables both solicited and unsolicited (offered) Windows Remote Assistance.
entries.rationale: Classic Remote Assistance is an unnecessary remote-control surface; the STIG rates it CAT I. Quick Assist is a separate Store app and is unaffected.

managedBy.groupPolicyPath: Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\System\Remote Assistance\Configure Solicited Remote Assistance

sideEffects: Classic Windows Remote Assistance (msra) invitations stop; Quick Assist is unaffected.

entries.title: Disable inbound Remote Desktop
entries.description: Denies inbound Remote Desktop connections to this machine.
entries.rationale: RDP is a top ransomware entry point. On a PC that never accepts remote sessions, denying connections removes the exposure entirely.

managedBy.groupPolicyPath: Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Windows Components\Remote Desktop Services\Remote Desktop Session Host\Connections\Allow users to connect remotely by using Remote Desktop Services

sideEffects: Users who rely on inbound Remote Desktop lose access to this PC.

entries.title: Harden Remote Desktop when enabled
entries.description: Requires Network Level Authentication, the TLS security layer, high encryption and secure RPC for RDP, always prompts for a password, and disables drive redirection and saved passwords.
entries.rationale: When RDP must stay on, these settings raise the bar against unauthenticated and downgrade attacks and reduce the data exposed to a session.

managedBy.groupPolicyPath: Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Windows Components\Remote Desktop Services\Remote Desktop Session Host\Security\Require user authentication for remote connections by using Network Level Authentication

sideEffects: Drive and clipboard redirection are disabled for RDP sessions; pre-Vista clients cannot connect (NLA).

entries.title: Harden WinRM authentication (client and service)
entries.description: Disables Basic, unencrypted and Digest authentication on the WinRM client and service, and disables the service RunAs credential store.
entries.rationale: Basic/unencrypted WinRM sends credentials in the clear and enables relay; disabling it forces Kerberos/NTLM over encrypted channels. The STIG rates the core settings CAT I.

managedBy.groupPolicyPath: Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Windows Components\Windows Remote Management (WinRM)\WinRM Service\Allow Basic authentication

sideEffects: HTTP-Basic or unencrypted WinRM to non-domain hosts stops working; use HTTPS with Kerberos or NTLM instead.

entries.title: Block inbound remote printing (PrintNightmare)
entries.description: Disables the spooler's remote RPC endpoint so this machine cannot accept inbound remote print jobs; local printing continues.
entries.rationale: The remote spooler RPC endpoint is the PrintNightmare RCE vector. Disabling it closes the inbound attack surface without stopping local printing.

managedBy.groupPolicyPath: Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Printers\Allow Print Spooler to accept client connections

sideEffects: This PC can no longer share its printers over the network; local printing continues.

entries.title: Restrict Point and Print driver installation
entries.description: Restricts printer driver installation from print servers to administrators, requires warnings/elevation, and enforces Redirection Guard and RPC privacy for the spooler.
entries.rationale: Point and Print without restrictions let a malicious print server push a driver and gain SYSTEM (PrintNightmare). These are the Microsoft-recommended mitigations.

managedBy.groupPolicyPath: Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Printers\Point and Print Restrictions

sideEffects: Standard users can no longer install printer drivers from print servers or network printers without an administrator.

entries.title: Turn off HTTP printing and print-driver downloads over HTTP
entries.description: Blocks downloading print drivers over HTTP, printing to HTTP printers, and web-services print wizards.
entries.rationale: HTTP printing and Internet driver/metadata downloads fetch content from untrusted hosts. Disabling them removes those download paths.

managedBy.groupPolicyPath: Computer Configuration\Administrative Templates\Internet Communication Management\Internet Communication settings\Turn off downloading of print drivers over HTTP

sideEffects: Web Point-and-Print and IPP-over-HTTP setups stop; device icons/metadata are not fetched from the Internet.

entries.title: Prevent standard users from installing printer drivers
entries.description: Requires administrator rights to add printer drivers to the machine.
entries.rationale: Printer driver installation runs privileged code; limiting it to administrators reduces a local privilege-escalation avenue. Mopria/IPP class drivers still work for users.

managedBy.groupPolicyPath: Computer Configuration\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Local Policies\Security Options\Devices: Prevent users from installing printer drivers

sideEffects: Standard users need an administrator to add printers that require a driver.

entries.title: Remove legacy network clients (Telnet, TFTP, Simple TCP/IP)
entries.description: Ensures the Telnet client, TFTP client and Simple TCP/IP Services optional features are not installed.
entries.rationale: These legacy clients speak unauthenticated, cleartext protocols and are common living-off-the-land tools. They are not needed on a modern workstation.
sideEffects: Only affects machines that actually use the Telnet, TFTP or Simple TCP/IP clients.
